title.narrative: Botswana National HIV/AIDS Prevention Support Project

description.narrative: The objective of the National HIV/AIDS Prevention Support Project is to assist the Government of Botswana to increase the coverage, efficiency, and sustainability of targeted and evidence-based HIV/AIDS interventions through: (i) strengthening the National AIDS coordinating agency's institutional management and coordination capacity; and (ii) financing strategic and innovative HIV/AIDS-related prevention and mitigation activities. It is envisioned that this project development objective would be measured by utilizing indicators addressing the longer-term planning, implementation, and effectiveness of national and decentralized coordination efforts. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is to support AIDS Coordinating Agency (NACA). The NACA component will provide very focused and strategic attention to build internal capacity to coordinate HIV/AIDS activities effectively, both for the project and the program more generally. The second component of the project is public sector ministries. This component will support public sector line ministries focusing on prioritized public sector mainstreaming initiatives in line with the national strategic framework. The third and the final component of the project is civil society organizations private sector. This component has been allocated the majority of the project funds, reflecting the importance of the civil society organizations in the achievement of project activities.
The revised project development objective is to assist the Government of Botswana to increase access to prioritized prevention services that reduce the risk of HIV transmission.

Number of male circumcision procedures performed in selected health facilities

comment.narrative:
(Note: This indicator had originally incorrectly been entered under the Intermediate Results Indicators, with respect to the project ISR.  It has been moved to be listed among the PDO indicators, as was its original categorization, as per the Projectppraisal Document.)
Total safe male circumcision (SMC) procedures completed since program inception is 150,136 which translate to 38.9% of the 385,000 program target, as reported by end-February 2015. A reported 1,776 of this SMC number are infants.  There were 32,527 SMCs done by all sites for the year April 2014 to February 2015, against 50,000 annual target, which is 65% achievement.

Number of organizational grants awarded that have been funded through the CFP mechanism

comment.narrative:
Note:  Calls for proposals were conducted three times to enrol qualified CSOs to participate in the project. In the first round in 2010, 16 CSOs qualified and they worked mainly in 4 districts. At the second Call, in 2011, 26 qualified in total. The third/last call was done in 2012 where 54 CSOs were selected to participate in 9 district and sub-districts. There were a total of 96 different organization grants made to 55 CSOsover the duration of BNAPS.  Given the capacity constraints among CSOs in Botswana, in its final two rounds of support, the BNAPS Project prioritized support to CSOs which had a track record for successful implementation and reporting, with a focus on CSOs committed to support the strengthening of smaller CSOs.
To minimize disruption on service delivery, NACA develop a mechanism to award multi-year grants to CSOs which demonstrated a strong track record in implementing and achieving results. This mechanism enabled seamless transition during annual implementation cycles and enabled continued coverage of services in targeted communities. This approach reduced transaction costs both for NACA and CSOs and enabled CSOs to develop a long-term focus on their programmatic interventions.

Health facilities constructed, renovated, and/or equipped (number)

comment.narrative:
This core indicator provides a measure of the number of primary health clinics that were upgraded/renovated to enable them to be compliant to administer highly active anti-retroviral therapy (HAART), as per the national ARV treatment guidelines.  As a reslt of its strong ARV program coverage, Botswana has achieved and sustained nearly universal treatment coverage (over 90%) -  despite recently expanding this no-cost program to cover to HIV+ individuals at earlier disease stages  (as per WHO's revised ARV treatment initiation recommendations).
(Note;  This indicator measuring the "number of primary health clinics upgraded and HAART compliant" was included in the PAD's Results Framework.  However, since the "core indicator" list was introduced in the Operations Portal subsequent to the project's Board approval, this indicator has been re-coded to indicate that it reflects a core indicator (as per the recommendation of AFTDE).
Source:  Ministry of Health HAART update reports

title.narrative: People receiving tuberculosis treatment in accordance with the WHO-recommended “Directly Observed Treatment Strategy” (DOTS) (number)

comment.narrative: The number of people receiving DOTS treatment in December 2012 was 6,829.  The strong referral program within the National TB Programme has enabled very high treatment initiation rates (100%).  Treatment success rates during this same period are noted to have been 79% (2009 baseline), rising to 81.5% in December 2011, and 74.8% in December 2012.

comment.narrative:
Percentage of young women and men aged 15–19 who both correctly identify ways of preventing the sexual transmission of HIV and who reject major misconceptions about HIV transmission” where the indicator is measured as a composite of answering &quotYes" to all the questions in the brackets  (Can the risk of HIV transmission be reduced by having sex with only one uninfected partner who has no other partners? Can a person reduce the risk of getting HIV by using a condom every time they have sex?) ; and two misconception rejections (1. Can a healthy-looking person have HIV? 2. Can a person get HIV from mosquito bites? 3. Can a person get HIV by sharing food with someone who is infected) to measure youth knowledge on HIV prevention).
Source:  Baseline data from BAIS II (2004) and current data from BAIS IV (2013)
